scope: Post-bootstrap Agent Operations & Observability installation only; no Doculyra product feature development
evidence: Complete supplied global Agent Operations & Observability addendum and Doculyra project configuration
AGENTS.md, CODEX.md, WORKFLOW.md, 04_USING_THIS_REPO_WITH_CODEX.md, framework manifest, project profile/team/state/queue and bootstrap report
All framework roles, capabilities, skills, protocols, tools, contacts, notification configuration and ledger
GitHub Issue/PR forms and conventions, protected-main configuration, CI workflows, live Issues and pull requests
Existing product observability standard and Azure Bicep Log Analytics/Application Insights/budget configuration
Installed Codex CLI 0.150.0-alpha.8 feature/config surface and official OpenAI Codex OpenTelemetry configuration documentation
Current environment model, deployment evidence, security/privacy controls and missing outbound email adapter status

dispositions.evidence: Bootstrap v1.1.0 is complete, validated and internally separated; observability adds policy, contracts, capabilities and gates without changing its authority model.
The provider-neutral product observability standard and Azure Log Analytics/Application Insights foundations are sound, but currently monitor product/dev infrastructure rather than agent operations.
No repository-queryable agent event store exists; a local metadata-only, closed-schema, Git-ignored store satisfies the approved minimal local/native mechanism without provider cost or lock-in.

Codex supports user-level OpenTelemetry and an interactive agents view, while project-local OTel routing is ignored and runtime_metrics is disabled in the observed CLI. Native export is documented but not falsely enabled.
GitHub Issues remains authoritative for work, decisions and defects and can be joined on demand without flooding Issues with high-frequency events.
Existing product telemetry rules already prohibit prompts/content/payloads; agent producers add closed-schema source rejection, secret-pattern checks, approved evidence hosts and local retention.
The exactly-once ledger and both event contracts are sound; the prepared ACS Email infrastructure still lacks a runtime adapter and delivery conformance, so autonomous execution remains blocked.
No new vendor is introduced; any future durable binding should assess the existing Azure route first and requires privacy/route conformance.

consultations: Delivery Orchestrator: bounded framework-only sequencing and Issue #11 evidence map
Repository Steward: versioned definitions, CI integration, runtime Git exclusion and reproducible commands
Architecture Guardian: reusable/project separation and provider-neutral event contract
QA & Release Lead: negative privacy, no-double-count, blocker/notification and environment evidence
Reliability & Operations: retention, locking, pruning, failure truth and existing Azure route
Security & Privacy: source allow-list, no raw prompts/content/secrets, destination activation fence
Agent Operations Lead: query model, attribution and quality-linked cost/performance analysis
risks: Exact native token, credit and cost data is unavailable; precision must remain UNAVAILABLE until a supported source is configured.
Native Codex OTel may include tool-result snippets or error details; export is ineligible without source/collector filtering and destination conformance.
The local runtime store is workstation-local and does not provide organisation-wide history; it is the approved minimal mechanism, not a durable external dashboard.

Product Authority blocking-decision and UAT emails cannot be delivered until the ACS adapter passes conformance; autonomous queue execution remains blocked without explicit GitHub-only fallback acceptance.
recommendation: Merge the privacy-safe local observability layer after independent QA, keep native/external export disabled, then implement and conformance-test the already selected ACS Email adapter or obtain explicit Product Authority acceptance of GitHub-only fallback before starting the autonomous product queue.
